title: The Man Who Saved 669 Children and Told No One for 50 Years #shorts
description:
He canceled his ski trip — and went to war without a weapon.

In December 1938, London stockbroker Nicholas Winton flew to Prague instead of the Swiss Alps. Jewish families were fleeing the Nazis, and no one was saving their children.

So he did. For nine months, Winton battled bureaucracy, raised money, and found British foster families for the refugee children. Between March and August 1939, he put 669 children on eight trains to safety in Britain.

A ninth train, carrying 250 more children, never left Prague. War broke out that same morning. None of them were ever seen again.

And Winton? He told no one. Not even his wife. For fifty years, his heroism gathered dust in an attic scrapbook — until she found it in 1988.

Then the world finally learned the truth: this quiet man had saved 669 children.
